TitlePage.Title: FusionSystems
TitlePage.Subtitle: Saturated fusion systems on finite p-groups
TitlePage.Author: Chris Parker
Jason Semerarosemeraro3733@googlemail.com
TitlePage.Abstract: The package implements the algorithms of Parker and Semeraro () for saturated fusion systems on finite p-groups in GAP 4: construction of fusion systems from generating automizers and from finite groups, computation of F-conjugacy classes and automizers, a saturation test, the isomorphism test and the classification of all saturated fusion systems on a given p-group. It incorporates the fast search for essential subgroups of Gautam () and replaces the fusion graph of by a lazy, graph free computation.

Chapter.Heading: Introduction
Chapter.Section:
Fusion systems
Let S be a finite p-group. A fusion system on S is a category F whose objects are the subgroups of S and whose morphisms Hom_F(P,Q) are injective group homomorphisms containing all those induced by conjugation in S, such that every morphism factors as an isomorphism followed by an inclusion. The fusion system generated by subgroups A_i \le Aut(E_i) (E_i \le S) is the smallest fusion system containing them. By the Alperin–Goldschmidt theorem a saturated fusion system is generated by Aut_F(S) together with the groups Aut_F(E), E running through representatives of the F-conjugacy classes of essential subgroups (the fully normalized F-centric subgroups E for which Out_F(E) has a strongly p-embedded subgroup).
In this package a fusion system is therefore given by the data
S, a p-group given as a pc group,
automorphisms of S which together with Inn(S) generate Aut_F(S),
a list of subgroups E_1,\dots,E_k of S (the essential subgroups) and, for each of them, a list of automorphisms generating Aut_F(E_i).
The fusion system is the one generated by these groups; it is not assumed to be saturated. Whether it is saturated is decided by .

Overview of the algorithms
Essential subgroups. By every essential subgroup of a saturated fusion system on S is S-conjugate to one of the subgroups C_S(xA/A), where A runs through the terms of a central series of S with factors of order p refining the lower central series and contained in [S,S], and xA through the elements of order p of S/A. These candidates are filtered with the tests of ; all tests are invariant under Aut(S) and the expensive ones (which need Aut(P)) are applied once per Aut(S)-orbit. The subgroup lattice of S is never computed.
Automorphism groups. Automorphism groups of p-groups are computed with the package autpgrp. If Aut(P) is soluble all computations with its subgroups take place in the pc group returned by PcGroupAutPGroup; otherwise a permutation representation is used.
Fusion. Let B = Aut_F(S) \ltimes S and let C be a p'-complement of Inn(S) in Aut_F(S). Every isomorphism in F is a composite of restrictions of elements of Aut_F(S) and of Aut_F(E_i^s), s \in S. The S-conjugacy classes of subgroups form the nodes of a graph which is built lazily: at a node with representative R and for every S-conjugate E^s of an essential subgroup containing R we record the Schreier graph of the orbit of R under Aut_F(E^s), with the arrows conjugated into the class representatives, and the arrows R \to c(R) for the generators c of C. By the Reidemeister–Schreier procedure for groupoids the F-class of R is the connected component of its node and Aut_F(R) is generated by the conjugates of the groups Aut_S(X), X a node of the component, and the loops of the component.
Saturation. By (which rests on ) a fusion system generated by Aut_F(S) and the automizers of F-centric subgroups is saturated if and only if Inn(S) is a Sylow p-subgroup of Aut_F(S), every fully normalized F-centric subgroup P is fully automized, and every fully normalized F-centric F-radical P has the surjectivity property: for all P < V \le N_S(P) the restriction map N_{Aut_F(V)}(P) \to N_{Aut_F(P)}(Aut_V(P)) is surjective. Let T be the set of subgroups of S contained in a B-conjugate of an essential subgroup. T is closed under F-conjugacy and under taking subgroups, and for P \notin T every F-morphism with source P is the restriction of a conjugation by an element of B (the automizers of the essential subgroups never apply). Hence the F-class of P, Aut_F(P) and the extension condition at P are those of the saturated fusion system F_S(B), and the conditions hold. It therefore suffices to run the test over the F-classes of the S-centric subgroups of the essential subgroups. These are found from the subgroup lattices of the groups E_i/Z(E_i), their F-classes and automizers from the lazy graph. This is how the package avoids the fusion graph of , whose construction (the subgroup lattice of S up to B-conjugacy and the Aut_F(E)-orbits of all subgroups of all essential subgroups) is the most expensive part of the original implementation.
Classification. follows : for each p'-subgroup K of Aut(S) up to conjugacy (Aut_F(S) = Inn(S) \rtimes K) the proto-essential subgroups are grouped into B-classes; the candidates for Aut_F(P) are the subgroups A of Aut(P) with Aut_S(P) as Sylow p-subgroup and A/Inn(P) having a strongly p-embedded subgroup, one for each Aut(P)-class (all conjugates of such a subgroup containing Aut_S(P) as a Sylow p-subgroup are conjugate under N_{Aut(P)}(Aut_S(P))), expanded to the conjugates whose Sylow normalizer contains Aut_{N_B(P)}(P), with equality when N_S(P) lies in no B-conjugate of a proto-essential subgroup; the subsets of proto-essentials and the assignments of automizers are run through up to the action of N_{Aut(S)}(Aut_F(S)); the resulting systems are tested for O^p(F)=F, O_p(F)=1 and saturation and finally reduced up to isomorphism. The automizer candidates are enumerated by the cyclic extension method with the hereditary bound |H|_p \le |Out_S(P)|; this is complete whenever GAP can handle the subgroup lattice of Out(P). For elementary abelian P with a huge Out(P) = GL(n,p) the package falls back to the monomial groups of the Aut_S(P)-invariant frames (and reports this through ), or uses candidates supplied by the user through the option candidates.

ManSection.Description:
returns the fusion system F_S(G) of the finite group G on a Sylow p-subgroup S. The underlying group of the result is the pc group Image( IsomorphismPcGroup( S ) ); the isomorphism is stored in the component F!.iso and G is the value of the attribute FusionSystemGroup. The essential subgroups are searched among the candidates of Gautam's theorem; with opts := rec( exhaustive := true ) all S-centric subgroups are examined instead.
gap> F := GroupFusionSystem( PSU( 4, 3 ), 3 ); <fusion system on a group of order 3^6 with 2 essential classes> gap> OutFSOrder( F ); List( EssentialSubgroups( F ), Size ); 4 [ 243, 81 ] gap> List( EssentialAutomizers( F ), Size ); [ 3888, 29160 ]
the group S, the prime p, the list of essential subgroups, the list of the groups Aut_F(E_i) (as groups of automorphisms), the group Aut_F(S) and the order of Out_F(S) = Aut_F(S)/Inn(S).
returns Aut_F(P) as a group of automorphisms of the subgroup P of S (for any subgroup P).

Section.Heading: Saturation, O_p(F) and the focal subgroup

ManSection.Description: OpF( F ) is the largest subgroup of S normal in S, contained in all essential subgroups and invariant under Aut_F(S) and all Aut_F(E_i); for saturated F this is O_p(F). FocalSubgroup( F ) is \langle [S, Aut_F(S)], [E_i, Aut_F(E_i)] \rangle, which is the focal subgroup of a saturated fusion system; O^p(F) = F iff it is all of S.
a central series of the p-group S with all factors of order p refining the lower central series, and the list of the subgroups C_S(xA/A) of Gautam's theorem.

returns a record with components autreps (representatives of the Aut(S)-classes of proto-essential subgroups), sreps (representatives of their S-classes), label and path (sreps[i] is the image of autreps[label[i]] under the automorphism path[i][1] conjugated by path[i][2]). With opts := rec( exhaustive := true ) all S-centric subgroups are examined instead of Gautam's candidates.
gap> S := SylowSubgroup( PSU( 4, 3 ), 3 );; S := Image( IsomorphismPcGroup( S ) );; gap> r := ProtoEssentialSubgroups( S );; gap> List( r.autreps, Size ); [ 243, 81 ]

the subgroups A of Aut(P) (as subgroups of the model group of FS_AutHandle( P )) containing Inn(P) with Aut_S(P) as Sylow p-subgroup and with A/Inn(P) having a strongly p-embedded subgroup, one for each Aut(P)-class. opts.candidates may be a function (S, P) returning lists of automorphisms (or model subgroups) to be used instead.
the p'-subgroups K of Aut(S) up to conjugacy, as records with components model and gens (the generators as automorphisms of S); Inn(S) \rtimes K runs through the possibilities for Aut_F(S).
whether the finite group G has a strongly p-embedded subgroup: with T a Sylow p-subgroup this is the case iff \langle N_G(T), N_G(Q) : Q \le T, |Q| = p \rangle \ne G.

ManSection.Description:
returns a list of representatives of the isomorphism classes of saturated fusion systems on the pc group S, by default those with O_p(F) = 1 and O^p(F) = F. The optional record opts may have the components OpTriv (default true), pPerfect (default true), OutFSOrders (a list of admissible orders of Out_F(S)), exhaustive (default false) and candidates (a function supplying automizer candidates, see ). Progress is reported at levels 1 and 2 of .
gap> L := AllFusionSystems( ExtraspecialGroup( 27, 3 ) );; gap> Length( L ); 4 gap> SortedList( List( L, OutFSOrder ) ); [ 4, 8, 8, 16 ] gap> ForAny( L, F -> IsIsomorphicFusionSystems( F, GroupFusionSystem( PSL( 3, 3 ), 3 ) ) ); true gap> Length( AllFusionSystems( ExtraspecialGroup( 343, 7 ) ) ); 13
The last example recovers the classification of Ruiz and Viruel for 7^{1+2}_+ (ten systems realized by finite groups and three exotic ones).
